news.title: Welbeck: 'It's such a privilege to play with these players'
news.body_en: Danny Welbeck has described playing with his Chelsea team-mates as ‘such a privilege’ and believes the Blues can achieve ‘something special’ over the coming years. Welbeck marked his Chelsea debut against Luton with a goal as the Blues reached the third round of the League Cup courtesy of our 2-0 victory at Stamford Bridge. The 35-year-old’s career has seen him represent England 42 times, win the title at Manchester United and lift the FA Cup twice during his time at Arsenal. He has played with some of the Premier League’s greatest ever players over the years but still appreciates being able to share a pitch with the likes of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Estevao Willian. 'It's such a privilege to play with some of these players and it's a joy when you're out there on the pitch,’ he said. ‘For me, playing as a nine today, it was more about staying on the last line. When the ball came into me, I was always ready to link up with the likes of Morgan and Cole. I really enjoyed that and I'm looking forward to it happening a lot more.' This summer has seen the Blues sign experienced players like Welbeck, Jordan Henderson and Maxence Lacroix, while continuing to add exciting talents such as Valentin Barco, Geovany Quenda and Marco Palestra to our squad. With world-class operators like Moises Caicedo, Reece James and Palmer already among our ranks, plus the addition of a title-winning manager in Xabi Alonso, Welbeck believes the Blues could have a season to remember. 'We can build something special here,’ he said. 'With the quality of players we have here, it's only right that we believe we can achieve something special. We'll keep pushing and working every single day, and we'll be trying to get those results at the weekends.' Welbeck signed for the Blues on August 1 from Brighton and Hove Albion, and started two games during our pre-season tour, before injury ruled him out of our season opener against Fulham on Monday night. He returned on Thursday night to make his competitive debut and had an immediate impact, linking up well with the likes of Estevao, Palmer and Rogers as the Blues laid siege to Luton’s goal. It was the striker who finally broke the deadlock early in the second half when he headed in Malo Gusto’s superb first-time cross. Welbeck said: 'It's really nice to get a goal on your debut and to get off the mark right from the start. So I am really pleased with that. 'More importantly, I'm pleased to get through to the next round and we've got to stand strong in every single competition this season.' The Blues had 26 shots on the night but had to remain patient as they searched for the opener, with Welbeck concluding: 'I think patience was really important. It's never easy against a low block, so you have to keep circulating the ball, moving it from side to side and looking for openings. 'In the first half, there were a few opportunities where we could maybe have got the first goal, but it didn't quite come. At half-time, the message was to get the ball into the box a bit earlier and put some crosses in. 'It was a good message and it worked well. Malo put in a quality delivery and I was there to nod it in.' Blues fans will be hoping this was the first of many for Danny this season.

news.title: Full Match: Chelsea vs Luton Town
Extended: Chelsea 2-0 Luton Town
Xabi Alonso on conviction, patience and learning from Luton victory
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso accepts Luton Town made it difficult for his Chelsea side to secure a place in the Carabao Cup third round, but feels the Blues gained valuable experience by breaking down a low block during tonight's 2-0 victory at Stamford Bridge. Alonso's side had to work hard during our first competitive home outing of the season. The Hatters sat deep and in a compact shape; it was not an easy evening. That was reflected in the fact that the game was goalless at half-time. However, five minutes into the second period, we broke the deadlock as a wonderful cross from Malo Gusto was headed home by Danny Welbeck on his Chelsea debut. Victory was secured as the game moved toward its conclusion. Estevao Willian played a key role in the goal, driving a shot toward the far corner that defender Hakeem Odoffin could only turn into his own net. Our win – and the manner of it - was vindication for the strength of the starting XI named by Alonso. He was not taking the Hatters lightly. 'We always want to choose a competitive team, he said. 'We are taking all the games seriously, and we are in a moment in the season where many things and processes are starting. 'I’m happy many players had their first minutes for the club, making their debut and playing their first competitive game in this stadium. It wasn’t easy - credit to Luton, as they made it difficult – but we played with conviction and patience, knowing the first goal was going to come in a moment, and Danny took it really well.' The post-match stats highlighted our dominance across the 90 minutes. We enjoyed 65 per cent possession, registered 26 shots, 45 touches in the opposition area and limited Luton to just one shot on target. It's why Alonso again described his side's display as 'serious' and emphasised how the game could prove beneficial for the Blues during the season ahead. 'For sure, it’s a performance to learn how to attack a low block. Against a 5-4-1, it’s not easy against any team from any league. We need to learn from today, as we will face this context in other games as well.'

news.title: Highlights: Chelsea 2-0 Luton Town
Alonso on Carabao Cup win 🎤
Welbeck reacts to debut goal
Match report: Chelsea 2-0 Luton Town
news.body_en: Danny Welbeck's debut header and an own goal from Hakeem Odoffin ensured the Blues booked a place in the Carabao Cup third round after overcoming Luton Town 2-0 at Stamford Bridge. Xabi Alonso, overseeing a competitive game in the Stamford Bridge dugout for the first time, named a strong side and the Blues controlled the contest from start to finish. However, the game was goalless at the interval despite several chances being fashioned. The deadlock was broken early into the second period – and it was a well-constructed goal. Estevao Willian linked up with Malo Gusto down the right flank, before the France international produced an inch-perfect cross for Welbeck to head home. Estevao was a constant threat and, with 11 minutes remaining, the Brazilian forced our second as his low drive struck the unfortunate Odoffin on its route to goal. We could have had more goals – Cole Palmer was denied on several occasions and both Morgan Rogers and Jamie Gittens hit the woodwork – but importantly the Blues have advanced to set up a third-round tie with Leeds United. Alonso included three debutants in his starting XI: Mike Penders, Valentin Barco and Danny Welbeck. They came into a strong side that also included Malo Gusto, Josh Acheampong, Maxence Lacroix, Pep Chavarria, Reece James, Estevao, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer. The game quickly settled into a pattern, with the Blues probing a resolute and deep Luton backline. Space was tight, but we carved our way through on multiple occasions. Palmer was first to threaten. The England international deftly exchanged passes with Estevao on the edge of the Luton area and whipped a shot toward goal. Josh Keeley saved and quickly reacted to deny Palmer on the rebound. From the resultant corner, Palmer dragged a shot wide. Gusto then fired a shot comfortably over the crossbar as we searched for the opener. Keeley was worked again midway through the half as, after Estevao had been fouled, James forced the Luton goalkeeper into a full-length save to keep out a free-kick. Our Brazilian winger then went close himself, driving a shot wide after a neat through pass from Barco. The visitors' threat was minimal during the opening 45 minutes; a header from Hakeem Odoffin that Penders easily saved was their best effort on goal. As the half moved toward its conclusion, we came inches away from breaking the deadlock. Estevao was once again involved as he broke beyond the Luton backline and cut a pass back to Rogers, who steered a volley against the crossbar. Rogers was involved in the construction of our next chance, showcasing neat footwork to evade two challenges and open up the pitch for Chavarria. The Spaniard played a pass to Palmer, but the striker's shot was blocked en route to goal. Come the half-time whistle, the Blues still had work to do. Alonso opted against any alterations at the interval – and the Blues boss was rewarded as his side opened the scoring five minutes into the second period. It was a well-crafted goal. The ball was worked to Estevao down the right flank, and the Brazil international stayed patient until the opportunity arrived to slip a pass through to the overlapping Gusto. He produced an excellent cross and Welbeck was perfectly positioned to head home. Luton attempted to rally, but they were largely kept at bay. The closest the visitors came to breaching Penders' goal were shots from distance from substitute Isaish Jones and Chelsea Academy graduate Kasey Palmer. Neither were on target, though. At the opposite end, Palmer's quest for a goal continued and our No.10 came inches away from finding the top corner with a powerful, curled attempt that flew just wide. Alonso turned to his bench with 23 minutes remaining; Jorrel Hato, Romeo Lavia and Pedro Neto were introduced for Gusto, James and Rogers. Joao Pedro replaced Joao Pedro soon after. The changes gave the Blues fresh impetus – and a second goal soon arrived to ensure our passage into the third round. Barco was instrumental, reclaiming possession in midfield and moving the ball to Palmer. He fed Estevao, who produced a quick stepover to shift the ball onto his right foot and drill a shot toward the far corner. His attempt struck Odoffin on its way to goal and ended the net. It proved Estevao's last involvement; he was replaced by Jamie Gittens before play restarted. The game was won, but there was time to add to the scoreline. Palmer continued to push for a goal and, as the game entered stoppage time, Keeley denied him once more and then stopped Joao Pedro's rebound. Gittens then went even closer, beating the Luton stopper but seeing his low drive strike the post. The third goal didn't arrive, but it didn't change the outcome. The Blues were through and, up next in the competition, come an old foe in Leeds United. The Blues go in search of our third victory in a week as we welcome Brighton and Hove Albion to Stamford Bridge on Sunday. The Premier League fixture kicks off at 2pm (UK time). news.title: Xabi Alonso on Blues debutants and a serious approach
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso says his Chelsea side for tonight’s Carabao Cup second-round tie against Luton Town, which includes three debutants, indicates how seriously the Blues are taking the competition. Our first outing in this season's competition comes at Stamford Bridge, as we welcome the Hatters to west London. Alonso has made five changes to the side that defeated Fulham on Monday evening, but the likes of Maxence Lacroix, Reece James, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers have all been named in the starting XI. 'We want to have a good start in the Carabao Cup after the Premier League,' explained the Blues boss. 'For sure, playing at home, it needs to feel good and hopefully it will be a good start here this season. 'We want to take all the competitions seriously – for sure, this season all of them are a target. For each game, we choose the best competitive team we think and this one is good enough to go through.' Penders, who was part of our squad at last summer's Club World Cup before spending the 2025/26 campaign on loan at Strasbourg, is handed his maiden outing for the Blues. And Alonso has enjoyed working with the 21-year-old Belgian so far. He said: 'We want that he enjoys [himself], that he has composure and maturity, that he gets used to playing in a new stadium with new team-mates. 'So far, he is very mature for his age – it was great that he played very competitive football last year in Strasbourg. Now this is the next step, and we need to help him.'

news.title: Matchday Unseen | Real Sociedad 🎥
Malo Gusto on fresh objectives and wing-back requirements
news.body_en: Malo Gusto is one member of the Chelsea squad with experience of playing in a system that utilises wing-backs, so the Frenchman knows exactly what is required of the role. Gusto lined up at right wing-back in our opening-day success away to Fulham, where it was quickly apparent how important those positions will be under Xabi Alonso. If you look at our first goal, scored in rapid time, Gusto is tracking the run from deep of a Fulham attacker when we recover possession. For our second, he is much higher up the pitch and plays the pass to Palmer that instigates the attack, with Fulham’s left side out of position as Antonee Robinson is forced to track Gusto’s movement. ‘It’s a position that I used to play before at Lyon when I was young,’ Gusto tells us. ‘So I know it and I do enjoy it. You need to bring a lot of energy – make a lot of runs forward and be there to defend as well. ‘You have to try to perform to your best on both sides of the games and it’s a good system for sure, but of course as a team we have to be prepared for anything.’ Gusto says he has enjoyed his time working with Alonso and there is great respect within the group for his achievements as a player and a manager. He has noted the ‘clear plan’ Alonso has in mind for his Blues team. On a personal level, Gusto benefitted from the break following the World Cup, where he helped France to a fourth-placed finish. Now, with three points already in the bank and with home games against Luton and Brighton ahead, Gusto is excited about the prospect of being involved in a special campaign at the Bridge. ‘It was good for the body to rest and I’m feeling really good now. I couldn’t wait to come back to Chelsea and just focus on our new objectives. ‘As a Chelsea player, of course we want to compete for the title and come back to the Champions League next season. ‘We have a lot of objectives and to achieve them we need to create a good dynamic as a team and see how it goes.’

news.title: Ellie Carpenter: Sociedad second-half display 'a hint of what's to come' from Chelsea
news.body_en: Chelsea kicked off the new season with a 5-2 win against Real Sociedad in the first leg of our Women’s Champions League qualifying tie, and with two assists to her name, Ellie Carpenter was one of the star performers on the night. The Blues went in level at the interval after Ainhoa Mari had put the visitors ahead with a stunning strike before Naomi Girma equalised. A powerful header from Veerle Buurman put us in front after the break, but Sociedad fought back with a determined equaliser, and it was at that point that Chelsea had to show what we were made of. Substitute Melvine Malard scored twice on her debut, and Lauren James chipped in with another in the final stages of the match to give us a three-goal cushion heading into the second leg. After the victory, Carpenter shed light on how we clicked into gear. ‘It is quite hard going straight into such a big, important game,’ said the wing-back. ‘Some of us are not really used to that. It was a good test for us, and obviously in the first half we were a bit rusty, and we had to fix things up; we really had to get into the game. ‘We came out in the second half and really gave it to them, playing with strength and confidence as well. It was a great team performance all round. ‘It’s also good to have these big games early on in the season. It gets us ready for the WSL, which starts next weekend. We have so many amazing individual players that can play in different positions. There's so much versatility in this team. We can play different formations. So that's also a strength of ours. Get your tickets now to welcome our stars home to Stamford Bridge on 5 September! ‘The opponent doesn't really know what's coming if we keep changing, but I think our fluidity, you could see, was slowly building. We're slowly building those connections, and it's only the first game of this season. ‘Our aim was to come out strong and score plenty of goals if we could. I think we did that as a team. We played the game, and it was fun doing it. I think it was a great performance and a hint of what's to come from this team.’ Sonia Bompastor was subject to a touchline suspension for Wednesday’s match. With the head coach absent, assistant Camille Abily presided over the 5-2 victory. Our Spanish opponents were well-organised throughout the first half, but the stand-in boss worked with the team on some tactical tweaks to iron out any issues. ‘I think at half-time it was just a case of keep doing our stuff, playing fast, playing with some discipline, and then it will come,' said Carpenter. 'The coach fixed a couple of things, and we did that, and we could see the results in the second half. We pushed them and got the win. ‘One of the messages at half-time was to hold our runs a bit more and make those forward runs connecting with the passes and the player, and just waiting for the right timing. We tidied that up in the second half and really exploited their high line. ‘It was a case of getting back on top and keep doing our jobs. We'll look at those goals we conceded and how we can tighten it for the next game next week.’ Having provided the cross for Malard’s second goal, Carpenter paid tribute to our summer acquisition. The pair have reunited after playing together under Bompastor and Abily at Lyon, and they linked up straight away. ‘Obviously we have that relationship from Lyon,’ the Australian smiled. ‘So it's nice to have her on the team. She brings such great energy and such a good vibe, and she’s an amazing footballer, so I like combining with her.’ Wednesday’s match took place at Plough Lane in Wimbledon, a ground that will play host to our Women’s FA Cup matches and any league phase games we face in the Women’s Champions League. All Women’s Super League fixtures will be played at Stamford Bridge, starting with a clash against Aston Villa on Saturday 5 September. Carpenter was impressed with our second new home and paid tribute to the support from the fans in the stands. ‘It's a really nice stadium, and it's a real football stadium,’ she remarked. ‘The seats are really close. You can feel the fans. They were really pushing us throughout the whole game. We're happy to move in here.’ See Ellie Carpenter and the rest of the CFCW stars at our new Stamford Bridge home when we take on Aston Villa! Click here to secure your spot...

news.title: Chelsea vs Luton: All you need to know
news.body_en: Chelsea host Luton Town in a 7.30pm kick-off (UK time) in round two of the Carabao Cup. Club historian Rick Glanvill and club statistician Paul Dutton look ahead to the Blues' first knockout tie of 2026/27. The fixture was moved to a less familiar Thursday slot to accommodate Monday’s trip to Fulham – a 3-2 Premier League victory for the Blues. This first-ever League Cup meeting between the two clubs is the setting for new manager Xabi Alonso’s official debut in front of the Stamford Bridge faithful – travelling Chelsea supporters have already chanted his name at Craven Cottage. The Blues are the capital’s most successful contestants in the tri-handled trophy with five wins, and we most recently contested the final in 2024. Back in December, our quarter-final victory at Cardiff City made it 19 straight wins against lower-league opponents in this floodlit trophy quest. The Blues then bowed out at the semi-final stage to eventual runners-up Arsenal. Luton’s greatest moment of giant-killing came in defeating the Gunners in the 1988 final of this competition. They last encountered top-flight opposition in the League Cup in September 2020, losing 3-0 to Manchester United – one of eight losses in the past nine encounters with top-flight opponents in this competition. Prior to beating Gillingham this month, the third-tier Hatters had been eliminated in round one of the Carabao Cup for three seasons in a row. All round-two games are broadcast live on Sky Sports platforms and this one is on Sky Sports channels 401 and 402, and their app. Wesley Fofana is suspended, while Xabi Alonso confirmed that both Moises Caicedo and Marco Palestra will miss Thursday’s Carabao Cup clash. Elsewhere, the Spaniard stated that goalkeeper Mike Penders has an opportunity to feature. ‘Let’s see, hopefully Moi could make it for the weekend, but we need to check a little bit more with Marco,' said Alonso in his pre-match press conference. ‘Otherwise everyone from Monday is okay, Cole [Palmer] is absolutely fine. Penders is part of the squad, so he has an opportunity. We will decide and then I am giving the team tomorrow to the players, so I prefer to respect that they know first.' In our history, Chelsea have exited at this stage of the competition on 13 occasions, though not since October 1995, to Stoke City over two legs. There were some memorable round-two matches in the early years of the competition, not least 3-0 away to Birmingham City on 23 September 1966, when Jim McCalliog became one of the club’s youngest debutants on his 18th birthday. The same month three years later, local visitors Charlton Athletic were thrashed 5-2 and the Blues also hit the bar four times. The clash with Sheffield Wednesday in 1970 required a replay, in which Dave Sexton’s regular ploy of throwing Dave Webb up front paid off. The utility man netted the winner for 2-1. In 1984, over two legs, John Neal’s side took what proved an unassailable 3-1 lead to Millwall’s Den, Kerry Dixon levelling in a 1-1 draw. We went on to reach the semi-finals. A shock 1-0 first leg-loss at York City was thankfully overturned 3-0 at the Bridge in 1986. The Londoners had a reputation for embarrassing defeats by lower league sides and rarely did that jinx hurt more than a 3-1 second-leg loss at Tranmere Rovers in 1991. A 5-4 aggregate victory over Blackpool in 1996 would prove our last round-two entry for 20 years, until a feisty Bristol Rovers outfit were edged out 3-2 on the Fulham Road, Michy Batshuayi bagging a brace. Our most recent match at the stage came in 2023, against Wimbledon. The Wombles took the lead through a penalty but succumbed 2-1 after a spot-kick in reply from Noni Madueke and an Enzo Fernandez winner into an empty net. Luton Town’s last win at the Bridge was through a penalty shootout in the little-regarded Zenith Data Systems Cup in February 1991. The Hatters’ most recent Fulham Road visit was a 3-0 Premier League loss in 2023, with Raheem Sterling (twice) and Nicolas Jackson finding the net. Chelsea are London’s most successful club in this competition, winning it five times, including the capital’s first and most recent successes.  Our ten League Cup final appearances is bettered only by Liverpool (15). Chelsea and Luton have met 47 times previously across all competitions, the Blues winning 21 of those encounters. We have prevailed in each of the past five meetings between the two on all fronts, starting with the 1994 FA Cup semi-final at Wembley. Chelsea’s record victory in this competition remains the 7-0 win at Doncaster Rovers on 16 November 1960, during our maiden League Cup campaign. Our two previous second-round appearances were also at Stamford Bridge, the 3-2 win over Bristol Rovers in 2016 and the 2-1 success against Wimbledon in 2023. Luton are playing their last few seasons at their quirky Kenilworth Road home, while a 25,000-seater stadium emerges in the town centre. Goal-line technology and VAR will not be in operation until the semi-finals, unless all host stadiums in the round are suitably equipped. Nine substitutes can be named and five used in the game (plus a concussion replacement if required). Yellow cards and suspensions apply only to this competition. Red card bans are served across all domestic fronts. Players are no longer cup tied if they move from one club to another during a transfer window. Each tie is decided on the night and extra-time is not used to decide ties until the second leg of the semi-finals.  In the event of scores being level after second-half stoppage time, the outcome will be decided by a penalty shoot-out.

news.title: Quenda on settling in England and first impressions of Chelsea
news.body_en: Geovany Quenda introduces himself to the Chelsea supporters with an exclusive interview in the programme for our first home game of the season against Luton Town in the Carabao Cup. The Portuguese winger made his competitive debut as a substitute against Fulham at Craven Cottage on Monday and tells us about his close friendship with Dario Essugo, the encouragement he has received from Xabi Alonso and the 'family' atmosphere at Cobham. 'We had a good pre-season and I think now it’s about making sure we also have a good start to the season,' he says of his first few weeks as a Blue. 'For me, I just need to help the team. That’s the most important thing – help the team to win. Of course, it’s difficult to come to another country, but this is my job.' Quenda also talks about his journey from Guinea-Bissau to the Premier League, via Sporting Lisbon, where so many other great players in his position emerged in the past couple of generations, from Luis Figo to Cristiano Ronaldo. We also delve into the distant past and uncover the long-forgotten stories of two Luton Town goal machines who swapped Kenilworth Road for Stamford Bridge either side of the Second World War. Joe Payne and Hugh Billington were two of the great goal scorers of their time, and we take a deeper look into their lives, with help from the research of Billington’s distant relative and genealogist, Kai Ridds. We also relive the 1994 FA Cup semi-final, when Chelsea legend Kerry Dixon came up against his former side with Luton Town at Wembley. Then there’s all the usual columns, news and stats, bringing you fresh insight and keeping you up to date with the latest goings on at the club. news.title: Camille Abily praises attack and gives fitness update on Naomi Girma
news.body_en: Chelsea assistant coach Camille Abily hailed our wealth of resources in attack as our new number nine Melvine Malard scored a brace on her debut in our 5-2 win over Real Sociedad at Plough Lane on Wednesday. The striker combined with former Lyon teammate Ellie Carpenter for her second of the evening, the pair having worked under Abily and head coach Sonia Bompastor at the French club in the past. ‘They know each other really well,’ said Abily, who was deputising on the touchline for the suspended Bompastor. ‘They also get on really well. They speak in French sometimes, so it helps because no one understands. ‘It would be great anytime we are able to score five goals. Of course, we have quality on the pitch, and also on the bench, because today the subs helped the team a lot. ‘Up front, we have Melvine. We have Mayra (Ramirez). She's not here yet, but I hope she will be soon. Aggie (Beever-Jones) is able to play this position. Last year, Lauren James played in this position. ‘That wasn't what we wanted, but when we are missing forwards sometimes we need it. Melvine is really versatile. She's able to play different positions and Aggie also, so it can help the team.’ Sociedad took the lead after just seven minutes, and fought back to level the scores at 2-2 before we extended our lead in the latter stages of the contest. Abily paid tribute to the opposition, and explained some of the half-time tactical tweaks she made to turn the performance around. ‘It was a tough game,’ she said. ‘Especially in the first half because Real Sociedad are a really great team, but I think we had a good reaction. We were so much better in the second half. There was also more space for us. So a tough win, but a good win. ‘At half-time we said we wanted to find and play in the spaces behind because their back line was really high. We score many goals like this, so this is sort of what we want to do, so it was good. ‘It was a good experience on the touchline. It was fun, but it's okay. Sonia can take the spot again!’ Finally, the assistant coach explained why defender Naomi Girma was replaced by Lucy Bronze in the second half. ‘It's more fitness,’ she said. ‘And also a decision because we have many good players on the bench, and we know with her calf we need to be careful. So for that, we didn’t want to take any risks.'

Match Report: Chelsea 5-2 Real Sociedad
news.body_en: Melvine Malard scored a brace on her Chelsea debut as we battled back to take a 5-2 advantage into the second leg of our Women's Champions League qualifier with Real Sociedad. It soon became apparent that Real Sociedad would not be easy to overcome as Ainhoa Marin scored with a stunning looping strike after just seven minutes. Naomi Girma then put us back on even ground with a header from a Katie McCabe corner, but the Blues went in at the interval with the scores locked at 1-1. The second half saw Chelsea emerge with renewed vigour, Sjoeke Nusken seeing her attempt ruled out for offside before young defender Veerle Buurman rose up to deliver a powerful header across the line soon afterwards. Our Spanish visitors fought back almost immediately, Cecilia Marcos' strike putting Sociedad back on even terms. That Sociedad were so determined made what happened next all the more impressive. An inch-perfect through-ball from Nusken picked out Melvine Malard, allowing her to slot home on her debut. Next came a wonderful run from Ellie Carpenter down the right as she then picked out Lauren James in the box and the forward made no mistake with her emphatic finish. An exceptional evening in Wimbledon concluded with our fifth goal. Carpenter once again powered down the flank, delivering a cross for Malard, who marked her first competitive appearance in Blue in some style. Head coach Sonia Bompastor was serving a suspension for this match, leaving assistant Camille Abily to take charge of the team. And the match began with Chelsea in firm control of possession and dictating the tempo of play. Yet, after captain for the evening Naomi Girma had confidently shepherded a through-ball into touch, it was the Spanish side who took the lead thanks to a moment of brilliance from Ainhoa Marin. The Sociedad number eight received the ball on the corner of the penalty area, lofting it over the outstretched Hannah Hampton before the ball nestled perfectly in the far corner, putting the visitors ahead with only seven minutes on the clock. Chelsea still had plenty of attacking intent, and Sandy Baltimore was unlucky not to level the scores when she smashed an attempt onto the underside of the crossbar. The woodwork then came to the rescue for the Blues at the opposite end when Sociedad fired another dangerous shot towards goal, but the offside flag soon went up. The equaliser came from a well-worked set piece. McCabe, on her full debut for the Blues, took the inswinging corner for captain Girma to flick the ball up and over the goalkeeper with a header with 30 minutes gone. Moments later, the Blues almost went ahead when Aggie Beever-Jones received the ball in space inside the box, but she dragged her shot just wide of the left-hand post. The Spanish side were providing a real test: well-organised, positionally disciplined and working hard to keep us at bay. For that reason, Chelsea went in at 1-1 when the half-time whistle blew, and there was more work to be done after the interval. Shortly after the restart, Sjoeke Nusken had the ball in the back of the net, but the flag was raised to swiftly rule it out.  And when James took a dangerous corner-kick, Buurman rose high above every player inside the box to nod down a pinpoint header to put us ahead for the first time in the contest. But that lead would last just four minutes when Marcos rifled in a right-footed effort from inside the box, and the scores were tied once more. Chelsea weren't done, though. When Wieke Kaptein laid the ball off for Nusken 20 yards from goal, the Germany international played a perfect through ball for debutant Melvine Malard, allowing the France international to round the goalkeeper and slot home. There was a sense that Real Sociedad were tiring, and when Carpenter powered down the line, her defender slipped at the crucial moment, allowing the Australian to pull the ball back for the onrushing James, who finished emphatically under the crossbar. Chelsea were now in the ascendancy, and substitute Maika Hamano was inches away from connecting with a pass that would've given the goalkeeper a stern test with ten to play. Taking a two-goal lead into the second leg would've been good enough, but an almost carbon-copy of James' goal extended our advantage even further. Carpenter advanced down the channel again, her pace beating her marker, when she squared the ball across the box for former-Lyon team-mate Malard. Our new number nine had a brace on her debut, a sure sign of things to come from the striker. We head into the second leg in San Sebastian on Wednesday 2 September with a three-goal cushion. We travel to Spain to face the return leg of this Women's Champions League qualifier against Real Sociedad, before we face Aston Villa at home on Saturday 5 September at Stamford Bridge, our first Women's Super League clash of the season. You can purchase your tickets for that exciting home game here. news.title: Under-18 Premier League Cup report: Wolverhampton Wanderers 0-2 Chelsea
news.body_en: Chelsea Under-18s began our U18 Premier League Cup campaign with a 2-0 victory over Wolverhampton Wanderers, as goals from Andrew Pennie and Heze Grimwade secured the win at the Sir Jack Hayward Training Ground. The Blues pressed with purpose from the opening stages and Pennie provided an early breakthrough with a powerful right-footed finish. Wolves continued to threaten, but Chelsea defended well when called upon and goalkeeper Jake Murray produced an important second-half save. Substitute Grimwade then doubled our advantage with 14 minutes remaining to complete the scoring. Chelsea created the first opportunity after five minutes. Yunus Linton's pressing presented Pennie with a chance in front of goal, but Alfie Arnold made the save. The breakthrough followed shortly afterwards. Pennie charged into the penalty area before beating Arnold with a powerful right-footed effort from a tight angle. Linton was among those to test the Wolves goalkeeper, directing a left-footed attempt towards the centre of the goal in the 38th minute, but Arnold kept it out. The hosts threatened at the other end moments later. Emmanuel Ayinde applied the defensive pressure required to prevent the Wolves striker from going through one-on-one. Pennie had the final opportunity of the half, sending a firm right-footed effort from outside the penalty area narrowly wide of the right post. The Blues continued to threaten after the interval and Linton forced another save with a left-footed strike in the 58th minute. Dan Hogan made three changes on the hour, introducing Trey Faromo-Adebayo, Grimwade and Bilal Shah in place of Linton, Pennie and Jack Anderson. Gabriel Sambou and Diego Chinyowa followed shortly afterwards. Wolves then applied a quick spell of pressure and Murray was called into action in the 71st minute. Our goalkeeper produced an excellent save to deny a close-range effort and protect Chelsea's advantage. Grimwade saw a shot blocked after receiving a good pass into the box from Shah, but the substitute was not to be denied. A minute later, Grimwade found space at a tight angle inside the penalty area and produced a composed right-footed finish to double the Blues' lead. The result gives Chelsea three points from our opening U18 Premier League Cup fixture of the 2026/27 season, to join Manchester United on maximum points in Group F. news.title: Alonso on a balancing act and team focus
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso explained why it will be vital for him to find the right balance to his team to face Luton Town on Thursday evening. Chelsea’s Carabao Cup campaign kicks off in west London tomorrow night, when we host League One side Luton in Alonso’s first competitive match on home soil in the Stamford Bridge dugout. Ahead of the second round tie, our Spanish manager was asked if he is likely to rotate his starting XI for this knockout game. It comes hot on the heels of Monday’s 3-2 win at Fulham in our opening Premier League fixture of the season, with the league visit of Brighton & Hove Albion fast approaching on Sunday. Alonso insisted he won’t be taking our Carabao Cup opponents lightly, ensuring that any rotation retains the right balance and competitiveness in the Chelsea line-up, as he plots our progress across three domestic fronts this season. ‘This season, knowing that we have time for all the competitions, every cup is important, every game is important,’ insisted Xabi. ‘We want to have the best competitive team to face Luton, with all the respect that everything deserves. And Luton are going to be the first game in the Carabao Cup. ‘The main thing is the quality of the players, that they adjust and that we have balance with the players around them that makes sense and makes the team better. ‘That is always my main focus, that the team is better with the qualities and knowing the best qualities of each individual player.’ During his pre-match press conference ahead of the Carabao Cup second round meeting with Luton, Alonso was also asked if he offered any specific words for Robert Sanchez in the last couple of days. It is clear that it is the team’s performance which is foremost in the mind of manager and players. ‘No, normal conversations,’ our manager responded. ‘We have talked more about team things, what we did well, what we have to do better. It was more about understanding the context of the game. ‘Every game is going to be important because we are in this process where we need to develop things, we need to make adjustments and we are more team focused.’

news.title: Xabi Alonso delivers the latest Chelsea team news ahead of Luton
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso confirmed at his pre-match press conference that both Moises Caicedo and Marco Palestra will miss Thursday’s Carabao Cup clash with Luton Town. The duo were both absent against Fulham on opening day, a game that the Blues won 3-2, and Alonso has announced that they will again sit out on Thursday - but Caicedo could return for the weekend visit of his former side Brighton. Elsewhere, the Spaniard stated that goalkeeper Mike Penders has an opportunity to feature, while he also expects Enzo Fernandez to be in the squad. ‘Not for tomorrow, both won’t make it [against Luton],’ Alonso said of Caicedo and Palestra. ‘Let’s see, hopefully Moi could make it for the weekend, but we need to check a little bit more with Marco. ‘Otherwise everyone from Monday is okay, Cole [Palmer] is absolutely fine. ‘Penders is part of the squad, so he has an opportunity. We will decide and then I am giving the team tomorrow to the players, so I prefer to respect that they know first. ‘Enzo, yes we expect him to be involved. He is training really well, he’s a good professional, and he will be involved.’

news.title: Chelsea vs Luton: Key statistics and facts
news.body_en: Chelsea begin our Carabao Cup campaign at the second-round stage, with a tie against League One Luton Town. Here are all the facts and figures you need ahead of the Hatters' visit to Stamford Bridge. Chelsea meet Luton Town for the first time since December 2023. Chelsea and Luton have never met in the League Cup before. We have faced them five times in the FA Cup, winning four, while our only Full Members’ Cup meeting ended in defeat on penalties. 	The Blues have won our past five meetings with Luton, starting with the 1994 FA Cup semi-final at Wembley. We then beat the Hatters in the FA Cup in both 2021 and 2022, before completing a Premier League double over them in 2023/24.	Luton’s last win at Stamford Bridge was 3-1 in September 1986 in the old First Division. Kerry Dixon scored our goal in front of just over 13,000 fans. news.title: Axel Disasi completes Crystal Palace loan switch

news.title: Chelsea’s fastest Premier League goals
news.body_en: Joao Pedro gave Chelsea an early lead inside the first minute at Fulham, adding his name to the list of the Blues’ fastest scorers in the Premier League. The Brazilian opened the scoring with just 31 seconds on the clock at Craven Cottage on Monday night, breaking clear from Cole Palmer’s flick to make a flying start to the 2026/27 campaign and set us on our way to a 3-2 victory. It was officially the earliest goal ever on the Premier League’s opening weekend, but only good enough to come sixth on the all-time list of Chelsea’s fastest goalscorers in that competition. Here are the five players who found the net quicker for the Blues in the Premier League… Chelsea blew Man Utd away on Jose Mourinho’s return to Stamford Bridge with the Red Devils. It was Pedro who got the ball rolling on the thrashing when the visiting defenders dawdled in a moment of miscommunication. There was no such hesitancy from our Spanish forward, who took full advantage to round the keeper and slot in. It wasn’t to be Chelsea’s day, as Arsenal came back to take the win at Stamford Bridge and go seven points clear at the top of the Premier League table, but we had got off to the best possible start. That came when Gudjohnsen showed his instincts in the box to control Geremi’s cross brilliantly and fire the opening goal past the keeper. Manchester United’s run of 29 games without defeat came to an emphatic end at Stamford Bridge, as Chelsea turned on the style. The Blues went on the attack right from kick-off, giving Dan Petrescu the chance to cross. When United goalkeeper Massimo Taibi came to collect but collided with one of his defenders, Poyet gratefully headed into the empty net. The Blues were heavy favourites against newly-promoted Nottingham Forest when we met at the Bridge early in the 1998/99 campaign, despite the visitors' decent start to the season. We underlined that status early on, though, with a goal all of Zola’s own making. It was his cross into the box from a throw-in on the left which created the chance. When Forest failed to clear their lines, the Italian was there following in on his own cross to place a first-time finish into the bottom corner. Chelsea had lost two home games in a row when Leicester came to Stamford Bridge looking to be the next visiting side to inflict pain on the Blues. This time we raced into an early, and unassailable, lead. An early foul gifted us a free-kick on the halfway line and Dennis Wise took the chance to run clear into space. He then picked out a teasing angled cross to the back post, where Spencer floated in the air to meet it and head down into the net.

news.title: Chelsea's fastest Premier League goals 💥
PGA South League report: London City Under-21s 0-8 Chelsea Women’s Under-18s
news.body_en: Chelsea Women’s Under-18s began their Professional Game Academy South League campaign in impressive fashion, securing an 8-0 victory away at London City Lionesses Under-21s on Wednesday evening. Chelsea Women's Under-18s, who play in the PGA Under-21 Women's League, were ahead inside seven minutes on Wednesday through Stevie Sinclair and established a two-goal advantage before the interval thanks to Maisie Brickell's strike. After the break, Chelsea added six more goals, with Chelsea N'Drin, Sinclair and Brickell all ending the match with two goals, while Jahyma Putman and Tess Finn also added their names to the scoresheet. Chelsea dominated possession throughout and combined attacking quality with defensive discipline to ensure they opened the new league season with both three points and a clean sheet. Chelsea made a positive start and moved in front after seven minutes. Victoria Rudz's clipped pass into the wide channel allowed Brickell to advance down the flank and deliver a cross into the box. Sinclair arrived from midfield and fired home from the edge of the area to give the Blues an early lead. The second goal arrived after 17 minutes and again involved Rudz and Brickell. Spotting space beyond the London City back line, Rudz played forward into the right channel, where Brickell drove towards goal before cutting across her defender and finishing at the near post. Chelsea continued to control possession and territory for the remainder of the first half, limiting opportunities for the hosts while taking a deserved two-goal advantage into the interval. A triple substitution at the break helped maintain Chelsea's momentum and a third goal arrived six minutes into the second half. After Putman switched play to Zoe Ciccardini, the defender found Sinclair's run in behind. The goalkeeper showed bravery to deny Sinclair's initial effort, but N'Drin reacted quickest to convert the rebound. Chelsea continued to press aggressively and nearly extended the lead further when N'Drin was brought down in the penalty area after a high regain. Sinclair's resulting penalty was saved, but the Blues were adding to the scoresheet once again soon after. The fourth goal arrived on 76 minutes when combinations around the edge of the box by Finn and N’Drin helped create space for Sinclair, who took a touch beyond the last defender before finishing confidently. A minute later Chelsea struck again. Finn recovered possession high up the pitch and switched play to Putman, who advanced towards goal before spinning past the goalkeeper and calmly finishing into an empty net. Finn then added her own name to the scoresheet on 86 minutes. After some quick combinations the ball was worked wide to Putman at left wing, she showed positive 1v1 play to get to the byline to pull the ball back to the edge of the box for the arriving Finn, who’s placed shot to the goalkeeper’s right added another. Three minutes later, N’Drin and Gregory helped win possession high up the pitch and the latter played into Brickell on the edge of the box. She turned and placed a composed finish across goal for Chelsea's seventh. There was still time for one more. Deep into added time, Sinclair dropped low to combine with Ciccardini, who was able to find Storey inside the pitch, with good vision and quick play. Storey played forward through the defensive line of London City Lionesses to find Brickell in the wide area. After some more positive play, Brickell delivered a lofted cross into the box which was met by N’Drin in the air to score the final goal. The result means Chelsea Women Under-18s sit top of the Professional Game Academy South League table thanks to their eight-goal winning margin. Chelsea's next fixture sees us travel to face Wycombe Wanderers Women in the senior Women's National League Cup on Thursday. The Blues then return to Professional Game Academy South League action on Sunday 30 August when Crystal Palace visit. news.title: Premier League ticket news: Hull at home - ticket application window closing
news.body_en: Ticket sales information has been released for our second home Premier League match of the season. The Blues host Hull City at Stamford Bridge on Saturday 12 September with a 3pm kick-off. Supporters intending to travel to or from this game using the London Underground are advised that planned engineering works may affect your journey. There will be no District Line service between Tower Hill and Edgware Road to Wimbledon, Kensington (Olympia), Richmond and Ealing Broadway stations. This means Fulham Broadway Station will be closed all day and there will be no District Line trains running to any nearby stations on that branch of the tube network. There is also no Circle Line from Edgware Road to Aldgate (via Victoria). Home tickets for members for men’s team matches are now allocated through a new application process. For each home match, eligible members have a designated application window during which they can apply for tickets. Applications can be made individually or as a group, provided all members of the group are eligible to apply during that window. Tickets will be allocated one per person with a maximum of four per application. Ticket application window opens – Friday 21 August 12pm Ticket application window closes – Wednesday 26 August 12pm The Ticket application window will be open for True Blue+, True Blue, CFC Blue, and Junior Blue members. As part of the verification process, a pre-authorisation charge £0.01 will be applied to validate your payment card. No money will be taken at this stage, and the hold will be removed by your provider. Tickets for this match are priced at Category B. Please click here for match ticket prices Tickets will appear on the Chelsea Official App prior to the event. Eligible members can submit their application through the ticketing portal at any time during the window, supporters must ensure they are logged in to successfully apply. Applying earlier does not increase the likelihood of success, giving supporters greater flexibility to apply at a time that suits them. As part of the new ticket sales process, members who are eligible for concession-rate tickets are automatically assigned their price class. To ensure you are receiving the correct ticket, please take the time to check the date of birth on your account is accurate. You will only be allocated tickets in your selected areas unless you choose to be considered for other available options. If you only wish to be entered for tickets in one area of the stadium, please leave the second option blank. Please read the ticket application information carefully before submitting your application. Successful and unsuccessful applications will be notified by email within four working days of the ticket application window closing date. Successful applications will be charged to their payment card approximately at this time. Supporters are not able to use account credit for ticket application window purchases. Tickets are for Chelsea supporters only. All persons under the age of 16 will be required to attend with and sit next to, a person aged 18 years of age or over. A maximum of four tickets can be bought per person, and only the ticket purchaser is required to be a member or season ticket holder. You are not required to be a member or season ticket holder to purchase non-Westview Club Chelsea packages. Club Chelsea tickets are non-refundable unless the match is cancelled, postponed, or moved more than 48 hours either side of the scheduled fixture date. All Club Chelsea ticket purchases are subject to Club Chelsea terms and conditions. For any further Westview enquiries, please email clubchelsea@chelseafc.com. Points will be added to eligible accounts following each game, provided the ticket has been scanned at the turnstile. This means that supporters purchasing tickets on the ticket exchange, or receiving tickets via ticket forwarding, will now receive loyalty points for attending matches. Supporters will receive three loyalty points for attending this match. Points will be applied after the fixture has been played.
